summary: All 31 runs use the same measured Grand Canyon crop through support/terrain.ts, and 27 of them already have per-frame update(), so the change to the pointer is mostly a matter of binding rather than rebuilding: only terrain-rgb-decode, terrain-ruggedness and topographic-position scrub by rebuild, and only peak-prominence, spike-repair and terrain-critical-points scrub a Data: knob. The visibility runs (viewshed, line-of-sight, point-horizon-profile, point-horizon-visibility) already write the observer column and row each frame, so 'place' costs only the binding plus a pointer-to-cell helper. The sun runs (relief-shading, slope-aspect-hillshade, solar-shadow-mask, terrain-cast-shadow) are natural 'aim' pads where angle maps to azimuth and distance maps to altitude, all per-frame today. The strongest posters are geomorphons, terrain-cast-shadow, solar-position and terrain-curvature. The weakest are cumulative-viewshed (towers clustered in one corner, most of the frame dark), peak-prominence and terrain-summits (scattered single pixels), profile-peaks (four profiles concatenated with full-height on/off bars), weiss-landforms (ten classes wrapped into the 8-colour default palette with no legend) and solar-irradiance (Swiss sun table over the Grand Canyon, saturated sun-hours). Two duplicate families hurt the catalog row. In the first, relief-shading, slope-aspect-hillshade, solar-shadow-mask and relief-blend all render as the same magma hillshade because there is no grey ramp. In the second, simple-local-relief, multi-scale-relief and texture-shading are all saturated red/blue diverging maps. Shared fixes in support/terrain.ts (a pointer-to-cell inverse, spread-out summit picking, and a grey relief drawer) and fixed ranges instead of 'auto' on five runs would lift about half of the group.

sharedChanges.change: Add getCellOfWorldPosition(terrain, world, x, y), the inverse of getCellWorldPosition, so runs that take the pointer can map it to an integer column and row (or snap it to the nearest summit/target) instead of percentage sliders.

Add findSpreadLocalMaxima(terrain, count, minimumSpacingCells): the highest maxima with a minimum separation. findLocalMaxima, which takes the highest first, clusters every tower and target on one plateau in the top-right corner.

Add drawRelief(terrain, values) that draws a [0,1] illumination or hillshade buffer in greyscale with smoothing. Today these fall back to the sequential magma ramp, so four different light operations look identical and none looks like a hillshade.

Add shared categorical palettes plus legends for the visibility codes (visible / hidden / out of range, with out of range transparent) and for the critical-point classes, the same way geomorphons passes categories.

Replace the default range: 'auto' with fixed physical ranges, for example sky view [0.5,1], openness [60,100] degrees, VRM [0,0.08] and standardized deviation [-3,3]. With auto, the per-frame zFactor, observerHeight and radius changes are renormalized away.

frameworkNeeds: pointer world position and the raster cell under it passed to update() and draw() (values.pointer), so a run can bind place/drag/aim/reach itself
cursor glyph layer: crosshair/dot at pointer, ring of a radius in world units, annulus (inner/outer radius), 3x3 or NxN box outline, eight spokes
sun-arrow glyph from the picture centre whose angle is azimuth and whose length encodes altitude
swipe curtain: draw layer A left of pointer x and layer B right of it, with a vertical line (render-only)
readback of one value (or a small slice, e.g. horizon[cell*directions..]) under the pointer for the readout text
GPU-reduced counts available to the readout (visible cells, visible targets, kept peaks)
highlight mask on a raster layer: emphasize cells equal to a category under the pointer, mute the rest
grey ramp kind for illumination and hillshade buffers
chart references: zero/horizon line, x tick labels (N E S W for azimuth), segment separators for multi-profile series
dots sized by a value buffer (drop, prominence)
debounced rebuild with snapped values, for rebuild-only props such as searchRadius, featureMaximum and validRange

issues.detail: findLocalMaxima picks the 8 highest maxima, and four of five towers sit together in the top-right corner while the fifth sees almost nothing.
issues.fix: Pick spread-out summits with a minimum spacing so the coverage overlaps across the frame.

issues.detail: Only the top-right quarter carries any count; the rest is dark context.
issues.fix: With spread towers and maximumDistance about 3000 m, the counts 1..N fill the frame.

proposal.binding: pointer cell -> the nearest tower's [column, row] in the observers buffer (the others stay); pointer distance from that tower is not used
proposal.glyph: the carried tower as a larger ring with a faint maximumDistance circle
proposal.readout: tower 3 [col, row] · cells seen by ≥2 towers 41%
proposal.feasibilityNote: observers is uploaded once in build; writing it in update with the pointer-carried tower is a small change (the count stays a rebuild).

issues.detail: Edge cells (form 0) are transparent, so a pale frame of context shows around the classes at card size.
issues.fix: Crop the drawn grid by skipRadius+searchRadius or draw invalid edge cells in the muted colour.

proposal.binding: hovered cell -> its landform; eight spokes of length searchRadius drawn from it, each coloured higher/level/lower using flatThresholdDegrees on the CPU elevation
proposal.glyph: eight spokes of searchRadius around the hovered cell, with all cells of the same form highlighted
proposal.readout: ridge · 3 up, 4 down, 1 level · searchRadius 12 cells
proposal.feasibilityNote: Forms are already written; the spokes are a CPU computation from inputs.elevation and the readout needs a value readback.

issues.detail: drawGrid has no range, so the zFactor scrub is renormalized after every run and barely changes the picture.
issues.fix: Fix range per output: sky view [0.5,1], openness [60,100] degrees.

proposal.binding: hovered cell -> its directionCount horizon angles read from the horizon buffer
proposal.glyph: a polar skyline star at the cursor: one spoke per direction whose length is the horizon angle, with the open sky as the filled remainder
proposal.feasibilityNote: The horizon buffer is allocated but not in outputs; expose it and read back one cell's slice.

issues.detail: No observer dot is drawn (only the converging rays hint at it), unlike viewshed and point-horizon runs.
issues.fix: Add an observer dot output like viewshed's observerDot.

issues.detail: Rays are context lines at alpha 0.5 and the 90 random targets are small, so blocked versus clear reads only from dot colour.
issues.fix: Draw the rays to blocked targets darker or omit them; enlarge the target dots and use fewer, terrain-meaningful targets (summits, rims).

proposal.binding: pointer cell -> observerColumn/observerRow (written as the observer half of every pair)
proposal.glyph: observer crosshair at the cursor; rays redrawn from it
proposal.feasibilityNote: update already rebuilds pairs and rays from the observer cell each frame.

issues.detail: No range is set, so the observerHeight scrub is renormalized away.
issues.fix: Set a fixed range for dominance (degrees) so a taller observer visibly brightens the map.

proposal.binding: hovered cell -> show the ring of ground it is compared against
proposal.glyph: annulus between minimumRadius and maximumRadius around the cursor
proposal.feasibilityNote: The output already exists; it needs an annulus glyph and a value readback.

issues.detail: The diverging range [-40,40] saturates most cells at exaggeration 1, so the map is near-binary red/blue.
issues.fix: Widen to about [-120,120] or lower the default exaggeration.

issues.detail: It looks the same as simple-local-relief and texture-shading (saturated red/blue).
issues.fix: Show what MSRM adds: a curtain against the elevation, or a radius-band caption from featureMinimum to featureMaximum.

proposal.binding: pointer x -> curtain between hillshaded elevation (left) and MSRM output (right)
proposal.glyph: vertical curtain line
proposal.feasibilityNote: Both buffers are outputs already; it needs the curtain capability (featureMaximum stays a rebuild slider).

issues.detail: The card scrubs 'Data: relief'; the operation has no props.
issues.fix: Use a probe on peaks instead of a data scrub.

issues.detail: On a 28-row grid, peaks are isolated single pixels, many on the frame edge, so prominence is invisible as a concept.
issues.fix: Draw peaks as dots sized by prominence and lower the default noise (20 m, the maximum) so only real peaks remain.

proposal.binding: hovered peak (nearest non-zero prominence cell) -> its parent peak and key saddle
proposal.glyph: line from the peak to its parentPeak, with the peak ring sized by prominence
proposal.feasibilityNote: parentPeak is written but not exposed; expose it and add nearest-peak lookup plus readback.

issues.detail: Nothing links a candidate to where it snapped, and the status colours have no legend.
issues.fix: Draw candidate-to-snapped segments and a snapped/unchanged/rejected legend.

proposal.binding: pointer -> position of one extra candidate written into the candidates buffer; it snaps live
proposal.glyph: a ring of radius around the cursor, plus a faint maximumMove ring and an arrow to the snapped summit
proposal.readout: snapped 230 m · Δh 18 m · radius 300 m
proposal.feasibilityNote: candidates are already rewritten in update; add one pointer-driven slot (count + 1).

issues.detail: The panorama bars have no horizon line or azimuth ticks, so they do not read as a skyline from the dot.
issues.fix: Add a 0° line and N/E/S/W ticks; draw it as a filled line rather than bars.

proposal.binding: pointer cell -> observerColumn/observerRow
proposal.glyph: observer dot with a faint maximumDistance ring
proposal.feasibilityNote: update writes the observers buffer each frame.

issues.detail: The 14 summit targets cluster in the top-right like cumulative-viewshed's towers.
issues.fix: Use spread-out summits.

issues.detail: Visible/hidden use default categorical blue/red with no legend.
issues.fix: Use the shared visibility palette and legend.

proposal.binding: pointer cell -> observerColumn/observerRow
proposal.glyph: observer crosshair; rays to visible summits solid, to hidden ones dashed or omitted
proposal.feasibilityNote: update writes observers, targets and rays each frame.

issues.detail: The four transects are concatenated into one line with no separators, and kept peaks are full-height 0/1 bars unrelated to the line.
issues.fix: Draw four stacked small profiles (or separators) and mark peaks as dots on the line at refinedIndex.

issues.detail: The noise slider is labelled 'Added noise' without the Data: prefix.
issues.fix: Rename it 'Data: noise'.

proposal.binding: pointer y over the chart -> minimumProminence (0–250 m on the profile's own metre axis, measured from the bottom)
proposal.glyph: horizontal ruler at the cursor with a vertical prominence bar of that length under each kept peak
proposal.feasibilityNote: minimumProminence is written per frame.

issues.detail: The VAT result is meant to be greyscale but draws with the magma ramp.
issues.fix: Draw it in greyscale (shared drawRelief).

issues.detail: It is indistinguishable from relief-shading, slope-aspect-hillshade and solar-shadow-mask at card size.
issues.fix: Greyscale plus a swipe or pad that shows the layers being mixed.

proposal.binding: x -> layers[1].opacity (slope), y -> layers[2].opacity (positive openness)
proposal.glyph: small 2D crosshair with the two opacities as axis ticks
proposal.feasibilityNote: All layer opacities are in the per-frame parameter buffer.

issues.detail: Shaded relief is drawn with the magma ramp instead of grey.
issues.fix: Use greyscale.

issues.detail: It is the same as slope-aspect-hillshade at defaults.
issues.fix: Raise the default skyViewStrength so the ambient-occlusion difference shows, and caption it.

proposal.binding: angle of pointer around the picture centre -> lights[0].azimuthDegrees; distance from centre -> altitudeDegrees (far = low sun)
proposal.glyph: sun arrow from the centre to the cursor
proposal.feasibilityNote: Azimuth is per frame; altitude is hard-coded to 40 in update and only needs to come from the pointer.

issues.detail: [-90,90] saturates at the default radius, so the map reads as binary red/blue.
issues.fix: Widen the range or make it scale with the radius.

issues.detail: It looks the same as multi-scale-relief and texture-shading.
issues.fix: The radius ring at the pointer distinguishes it.

proposal.binding: pointer y -> radius (1–20 cells, bottom small); the ring is drawn at the pointer position
proposal.glyph: circle of radius at the cursor showing the window whose mean is subtracted
proposal.readout: radius 8 cells (≈ 700 m) · relief here +34 m
proposal.feasibilityNote: radius is written per frame (maximumRadius 20 at construction).

issues.detail: The hillshade draws with the magma ramp rather than grey.
issues.fix: Greyscale for hillshade.

issues.detail: Only the hillshade output is shown on the poster, the same picture as relief-shading.
issues.fix: Show slope or aspect beside the hillshade, for example as a swipe with the cyclic aspect wheel.

proposal.binding: angle around the centre -> azimuthDegrees; distance from centre -> altitudeDegrees (5–85°, far = low)
proposal.glyph: sun arrow from the centre
proposal.feasibilityNote: Both are written by update.

issues.detail: The sun table uses longitude 7.9 and latitude 46.5 (the Alps) over a Grand Canyon DEM (about 36.1°N, 112.1°W).
issues.fix: Default to the DEM's own latitude and longitude.

issues.detail: At June and 46.5°, sun hours nearly fill the [0,14] range, so the map is washed-out pale.
issues.fix: Default to a winter month where canyon shadowing dominates, or range [0,16] with a midpoint.

issues.detail: The insolation output uses 'auto', so month and latitude changes are renormalized away.
issues.fix: Use a fixed kWh/m² range.

proposal.binding: x -> sunTable month (Jan..Dec), y -> sunTable latitude (top = north)
proposal.glyph: month tick along the bottom and a latitude tick on the left edge at the cursor
proposal.feasibilityNote: The sun table is recomputed and written in update.

proposal.binding: pointer = the subsolar point: x longitude -> hour UTC (12 - longitude/15), y latitude clamped to ±23.4° -> date by solar declination (month, first-half-year branch)
proposal.glyph: sun disc at the cursor with the terminator following it
proposal.feasibilityNote: The timestamp is per frame; update needs a declination-to-date mapping instead of an integer month.

issues.detail: Illumination draws in magma, not grey.
issues.fix: Greyscale.

issues.detail: At altitude 25° it looks like a plain hillshade (relief-shading, slope-aspect-hillshade); the cast shadows that make it different are faint.
issues.fix: Lower the default altitude to about 10° or draw sunVisibility as a shadow overlay.

proposal.binding: angle around the centre -> azimuthDegrees; distance from centre -> altitudeDegrees (3–80°, far = low)
proposal.glyph: sun arrow from the centre
proposal.feasibilityNote: Both values are in the per-frame parameter buffer; the horizon is precomputed.

issues.detail: The card scrubs 'Data: spikes'; jump and tolerance are rebuild-only.
issues.fix: Use a swipe between the damaged and repaired tiles.

issues.detail: At the defaults, four damaged blocks still show as dark squares in the 'repaired' output, so the poster reads as a failed repair.
issues.fix: Check that jump 200 / tolerance 40 repair the ±512 m blocks, or drop the 2-step offsets from the demo damage.

proposal.binding: angle around the centre -> azimuthDegrees; distance from centre -> altitudeDegrees (3–60°, far = low)

issues.fix: Make the lines thicker and brighter, and colour them by level on a sequential ramp.
